subject: Post-demo: recommended model variants & evaluation pack (regression questions)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@clearledger.com>, Cara Lim <cara.lim@clearledger.com>
Cc: security@clearledger.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended model variants & evaluation pack (regression questions)

Hi Sam / Cara —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Solid conversation and very helpful context on the fraud-detection edge cases you care about. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

1) Evaluation pack attached: clearledger_eval_pack_v1.zip (includes benchmark outputs, prompt sets, and sample traces). The short README highlights the three workload slices we focused on: (a) short transactional labels, (b) multi-turn anomaly explanations, (c) high-entropy user-initiated queries.

2) Recommended serving variants: 
- rwd-llama-70b-int8 (best latency/cost balance for your throughput)
- rwd-llama-70b-std (higher-quality, fallback for high-risk cases)
- rwd-13b-q4 (cheap baseline for low-risk bulk scoring)

3) Immediate asks from ClearLedger: you flagged concern about output drift after the vendor model update last week. We included a diff report sample in model_diff_report.pdf and the prompt_set_v2.txt so you can reproduce.

4) Proposed next steps:
- Technical review: schedule a 60-min session with your engineers and our inference team (Aditya + Marcus).
- Temporary mitigation: we can pin to the last verified model variant in your Dedicated pool while we triage diffs.
- Action items for us: attach the eval pack, prompt set, and a short runbook for quick rollback.

Could you confirm availability for a technical deep-dive next week (Mon/Tue preferred)? Also let us know which example traces from the pack you want prioritized.

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0179
attachments: clearledger_eval_pack_v1.zip; prompt_set_v2.txt; model_diff_report.pdf
From: Sam Park <sam.park@clearledger.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Lim <cara.lim@clearledger.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model variants & evaluation pack (regression questions)

Tessa —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the eval pack. I pulled the diff PDF this morning; a few questions before we bring our infra folks into the call: 

- How large were the behavioral deltas you saw between rwd-llama-70b-int8 and the updated vendor variant (percent of responses with label flips)? Any examples you can point to in the pack that show regression on our high-risk slice?
- If we pin to a previous variant, what is the expected operational impact on latency and cost? We currently run 600 TPS at peak.
- Our security team wants to know whether the update could affect prompt-based filtering — they asked to loop in security@clearledger.com.

We can do Mon 14 Jun 9–11am PT or Tue 15 Jun 1–3pm PT for the deep dive. If pinning introduces noticeable latency, we may prefer a fallback routing approach.

—Sam
Sam Park
Head of Fraud Analytics, ClearLedger
sam.park@clearledger.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@clearledger.com>, Cara Lim <cara.lim@clearledger.com>, security@clearledger.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: recommended model variants & evaluation pack (regression questions) — need quick triage

Aditya / Marcus —

Looping you in on ClearLedger's thread. They saw behavioral diffs after the upstream update and have asked for concrete numbers and a recommended mitigation. I attached the eval pack and model_diff_report.pdf which contains a small set of pairs where label flips occurred on the high-risk slice. Highlights: ~4.8% flip rate on the high-risk tests between our verified variant and the new vendor build; flips concentrated on multi-turn contextual checks (see folder /high-risk/contextual).

What I need from you for the technical deep-dive (Tue 15 Jun 1–3pm PT preferred):
- Quick regression triage: confirm flip rate and whether pinning to the previous variant (rwd-llama-70b-int8@v20270601) is safe operationally.
- If pinning is risky, propose fallback: e.g., route high-risk traffic to rwd-llama-70b-std or use a short prompt-filter that blocks ambiguous outputs.
- One-slide summary we can send to Sam ahead of the call plus the short runbook_quickfix.md for on-call engineers.

Attaching: clearledger_eval_pack_v1.zip, prompt_set_v2.txt, model_diff_report.pdf, runbook_quickfix.md

Thanks —
Tessa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Sam Park <sam.park@clearledger.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Cara Lim <cara.lim@clearledger.com>, security@clearledger.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model variants & evaluation pack (regression questions) — triage and short-term plan

Tessa / Sam —

Thanks for the materials; reproduced the diffs and ran a quick cross-check on the high-risk slice. Short summary for the call and next actions: 

1) Reproduction and numbers:
- Confirmed ~4.6% label flip rate between rwd-llama-70b-int8@v20270601 and the new vendor build (sample size = 1,200 high-risk examples). See attached model_diff_report.pdf for paired examples and a small confusion matrix.

2) Operational impact:
- Pinning to v20270601: latency delta ~+12ms p50 on your Dedicated GPU pool; cost delta negligible (~1.5% uplift due to slightly different kernel path). For 600 TPS peak, we estimate an additional 0.8 GPU-hours/day if pinned (we'll provide an exact run-rate once we pull your telemetry).

3) Recommendation (short-term):
- Pin production to rwd-llama-70b-int8@v20270601 for the next 72 hours while we run a targeted regression patch. This gives ClearLedger immediate stability on the high-risk slice.
- Add a lightweight prompt-filter for ambiguous classifications as a precaution (we included prompt_set_v2.txt with filter templates).
- Configure fallback routing: route flagged high-risk requests to rwd-llama-70b-std (higher-quality) automatically if confidence < 0.7.

4) Communication and runbook:
- I've drafted runbook_quickfix.md (attached) with commands to pin, unpin, and switch fallback routing. We'll also produce a one-slide summary for your execs before the call.

5) Next steps / schedule:
- We can execute the pin during your low-traffic window tonight (requested window: 11pm–1am PT). Please confirm.
- Technical deep-dive: Tue 15 Jun 1:30–2:30pm PT (this timing is tight but works for our infra folks). Confirmed attendees: Aditya, Marcus, Tessa, Sam, Cara.

If you want an alternative to pinning, we can instead put an automated canary: 95% production -> new build, 5% -> pinned variant until patch is validated. That reduces blast radius but delays full mitigation.

Happy to walk through the report in the call.

—Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
attachments: model_diff_report.pdf; runbook_quickfix.md; prompt_set_v2.txt
